title: Conductors, Insulators and Simple Circuits
seo_title: Grade 5 Science: Conductors, Insulators and Simple Circuits Worksheets (MATATAG)
standard_code: Grade 5, Quarter 3: Force, Motion, and Energy
standard_text: A simple circuit needs a source of energy (cell), wires and a load (bulb) in a closed loop; conductors let electricity flow and insulators do not; electricity must be used safely. (summary of the MATATAG Science curriculum, Grade 5, Quarter 3: Force, Motion, and Energy)
meta_desc: Free Grade 5 Science worksheets (MATATAG, Quarter 3: Force, Motion, and Energy): parts of a circuit, circuit symbols, will it light?, conductors and insulators and using electricity safely. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Electricity flows only in a complete circuit.
key_sub: Conductors let electricity through; insulators do not.
body_html:
How to think about it

A circuit has a cell (energy source), wires (conductors) and a bulb, buzzer or motor (load) joined in a complete loop. A switch opens the circuit (off) and closes it (on). Circuits are drawn with symbols.

Metals such as copper are conductors; plastic, rubber, wood and glass are insulators. Mains electricity from the wall is much stronger than a cell and can kill. Never touch plugs with wet hands, never overload plugs and stay away from illegal connections and fallen power lines.

Example

A paper clip is put in a gap in a circuit and the bulb lights. Is it a conductor?

Electricity flows through it.

Answer: yes

Example

What happens when a switch is opened?

The loop is broken.

Answer: the bulb goes off

Common mistakes

  • Thinking a bulb lights with one wire to the cell.
  • Thinking water is a safe insulator.
  • Thinking mains electricity is as safe as a flashlight cell.

items.q: Why is plugging too many appliances into one socket dangerous?
c: Bare wires could give an electric shock or cause a short circuit.
The cable overheats and could start a fire.
It conducts electricity to your body, giving a shock.
If a live wire touches the metal case, the case could give a shock.
items.e: The cable overheats and could start a fire.

items.q: An air-conditioner of power 1.5 kW is used for 10 hours. Electricity costs 35 cents per kWh. What is the cost?
items.e: Energy = 1.5 kW × 10 h = 15 kWh; cost = 15 × 35 = 525 cents.
